searchText: guys I have a simplifying proposal for validator custody, kindly review/feedback: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4154 left some comments peerdas-devnet-5 is now finalizing again. <@498331483732312075> cpu usage has been 100% on grandine node since the restart did you rebuild the image? it spike at start, and should be relax after that ah yeah rolling it out now. spike is still present https://grafana.observability.ethpandaops.io/d/MRfYwus7k/nodes?orgId=1&var-consensus_client=All&var-execution_client=All&var-network=peerdas-devnet-5&var-filter=ingress_user%7C%21~%7Csynctest.%2A can I have access to grafana dashboard? need to optimize requests load we are back 🙂 4/4 proposing now and 4/4 went through one round of genesis sync <@592004585506340885> <@427491045308235776> <@520034910149410861> <@531934490826768418> 1. regarding `compute_cells` function, I see that it's been added to `c-kzg-4844` repo, but I'm curious is there any efforts needed to implement it in https://github.com/crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844 or other languages library? 2. for variables like `CellsPerExtBlob`, it looks like it is only defined in ckzg lib for now, seems like we need to define them in go-kzg as well? 3. can we publish a release for c-kzg library? currently I'm using the latest commit for including new `compte_cells` code Let me know if my understanding is incorrect, I'm trying to implement cell proof related migration feature in geth, and geth seems to be solely relying on go-kzg, while prysm currently relies on c-kzg, and go-kzg does not seem to be ready Hey there, thanks for bringing this up. The other libraries have been updated too; but go-kzg-4844 has been deprecated and moved to go-eth-kzg (https://github.com/crate-crypto/go-eth-kzg). go-eth-kzg was updated here (https://github.com/crate-crypto/go-eth-kzg/commit/37673f594ad507e6b6faaad7934feef8472002f4) and rust-eth-kzg was updated here (https://github.com/crate-crypto/rust-eth-kzg/pull/300). And yes, I can make a new ckzg release soon. I've been waiting for a PR to add elixir bindings to be merged. Were the experiments in the network limit devnets doc (https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/network-limit-devnets) done manually or were they scripted? If they were scripted, I'd love to build on top of them!
